thought
I have viewed the first reference images for Anthracnose (`PlantWild_26.jpg`) and Cigar_End_Rot (`PlantWild_30.jpg`).

The Anthracnose reference image shows several yellow bananas with prominent dark brown to black irregular patches and sunken areas, very similar to the test image.

The Cigar_End_Rot reference image shows a green banana with a blackened, shriveled end, consistent with the "cigar end" description. This does not match the test image.

Based on this visual comparison, Anthracnose is a much stronger match for the test image. I've used 2 out of 8 reference image views. I will now view reference images from the remaining 5 possible classes, even though they are for different plant parts, to ensure I'm not missing any visual similarities (as per the "explore before confirming" instruction). I will prioritize one reference image per remaining class that affects the leaf or whole plant. Since the test image is a pod, I will keep in mind that these might not be directly comparable.

I will view one image from each of the remaining 5 classes:
1. Banana_Bunchy_Top_Virus (leaf)
2. Bunchy_Top (leaf)
3. Cordana_Leaf_Spot (leaf)
4. Panama_Disease (leaf)
5. Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka (leaf)

This will use 5 more views, bringing my total to 7/8.

thought
I have viewed one reference image from each of the remaining 5 classes (Banana_Bunchy_Top_Virus, Bunchy_Top, Cordana_Leaf_Spot, Panama_Disease, and Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka).

None of these leaf-based diseases show symptoms that resemble the dark, sunken lesions on the banana fruit in the test image. The images show various leaf discolorations, streaking, and wilting, which are distinct from the fruit rot observed.

Given that Anthracnose was a strong visual match in the initial comparison and these other diseases do not match at all, my confidence in Anthracnose is very high. I have used 7 out of 8 reference images. I will use the last view to look at another Anthracnose image to solidify the confidence.
